sentences.text: Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 5401 of 2023

Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Akhilesh Kumar Shukla,Ravi Shankar Mishra Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
This anticipatory bail application (under section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No.133 of 2017, under Sections 406, 420, 465 I.P.C., Police Station Nakhasa, District Sambhal.
It is submitted that in this case applicant is innocent and has committed no offence.
It is further submitted that there is nothing on record to show the complicity of the present applicant in the present case.

It is also submitted that all the offences said to be committed are punishable with sentence less than 7 years even though the Investigating Officer is trying to arrest the applicant,

sentences.text: therefore, the applicant is under apprehension of imminent arrest.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the investigation.

Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail and urged that in this case all the offences said to have been committed by the applicant are punishable with sentence less than 7 years regarding which protection u/s 41A Cr.P.C. is available to the applicant, therefore, there is no any apprehension of arrest of the applicant by the police.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perusal of record, it appears that all the offences said to be committed by the applicant are punishable with sentence less than 7 years regarding which protection u/s 41A Cr.P.C. is already available to the applicant, therefore, there may be no apprehension of arrest against the applicant by the police.

Accordingly, this anticipatory bail application is disposed of finally in view of the protection as provided u/s 41, 41A, 60A and interpreted by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar vs. State of Bihar (2014) 8 SCC 273 and again reiterated in the case of Satender Antil vs.
Central Bureau of Investigation and another LL 2022 SC 577 decided on 11.07.2022 according to which the Investigating Agency is duty bound to comply with the mandate of Section 41 and 41-A Cr.P.C. and any dereliction of their part has to be brought to be notice of higher authorities by the courts followed by appropriate action.
Order Date :- 22.5.2023
